gaps.sentence: The hotel was full, so we had to look for ___ hotel.
gaps.explanation: 'Another hotel' means some other, unspecified one; 'the other hotel' would imply exactly two known hotels.

gaps.sentence: She spent a great ___ of time preparing the report.
gaps.hint: fixed phrase: a great ___ of + uncountable
gaps.explanation: 'A great deal of time' is used with uncountable nouns; 'a great number of' needs a countable plural.

gaps.sentence: There are two cafes here, but ___ of them is open on Mondays.
gaps.explanation: 'Neither of them is open' is correct for two items with a singular verb; 'both' and 'all' would need 'are'.

gaps.hint: price per item comes at the end
gaps.explanation: 'Fifteen pounds each' means fifteen pounds per ticket; 'every' cannot stand alone in this position.

gaps.sentence: Only ___ people attended the talk, which was disappointing.
gaps.hint: countable plural; 'only a few' is the natural pattern
gaps.explanation: 'Only a few people' is the standard way to say a small number; 'only few' is not used.

gaps.sentence: She made very ___ mistakes in the essay, so she nearly got full marks.
gaps.explanation: 'Very few mistakes' means almost none, which explains the high mark; 'mistakes' is countable.

gaps.sentence: Don't rush — we've got ___ of time.
gaps.hint: fixed pattern: ___ of time (no article needed)
gaps.explanation: 'Plenty of time' needs no article; 'lot of time' would need 'a', and 'much of time' needs 'the'.

gaps.sentence: Three of the six books were mine; ___ were my sister's.
gaps.hint: the defined remainder of a set of six
gaps.explanation: 'The others' refers to the specific remaining books in the known set of six.
